title: Are Large Language Models Strategic Decision Makers? A Study of Performance and Bias in Two-Player Non-Zero-Sum Games

model.params_source: paper Technical Appendix B (Answer-Only prompting tested at T = 1.0); max_tokens and top_p assumed

task.subset_rule: all: the 8 Stag Hunt A->B setups (Table 6 configs 1 and 2, where A is listed first, x the four preference pairs (AP, FP) in {CG, SG}^2), 100 runs each, Answer-Only prompt
task.approximation: the preference sentences are printed as template slots ('acting agent's preferred behaviour (CG v SG)'); filled as 'prioritise Common-Gain' / 'prioritise Self-Gain' following the paper's wording; Table 1 pools the A->B setups, so the config pools the 800 runs; the statistic is computed as accuracy against the constant gold 'A' (share of runs choosing A); replies without a parsable action count as non-A instead of being dropped from the denominator

items.source: Technical Appendix B: BASE PROMPT, Action-Only PROMPT, Table 6 (Stag Hunt payoff matrices per configuration), preference combinations
items.config_or_split: Stag Hunt, configurations 1 and 2 (A->B order), AO prompting; config 1: PO(A,A)=5 PO(A,B)=0 PO(B,A)=4 PO(B,B)=2; config 2: PO(A,A)=2 PO(A,B)=4 PO(B,A)=0 PO(B,B)=5

fields_prose.input: payoff configuration (1 or 2) and preference pair (AP, FP)
fields_prose.label: none (the statistic is the frequency of choosing A)

prompt.source_location: Technical Appendix, Section B (BASE PROMPT + Action-Only PROMPT); payoffs from Table 6
prompt.verbatim: partial: BASE PROMPT and Action-Only PROMPT copied verbatim with the paper's 'label 1 / label 2 / PO(...)' slots turned into placeholders and the JSON's typographic quotes replaced by straight quotes; the two preference sentences are reconstructed from the slot description

placeholders_prose.label_1: 'A' (A->B order: A is the first-listed action label)
placeholders_prose.po_11: PO(A,A) from Table 6 for the configuration (5 in config 1, 2 in config 2)
placeholders_prose.po_12: PO(A,B): payoff to the player choosing A when the other chooses B (0 in config 1, 4 in config 2)
placeholders_prose.ap_pref: acting player's preferred behaviour: 'prioritise Common-Gain' or 'prioritise Self-Gain'
placeholders_prose.fp_pref: fellow player's preferred behaviour: 'prioritise Common-Gain' or 'prioritise Self-Gain'

output.postprocess: strip, uppercase; replies with no A/B are counted as invalid and excluded from the denominator (their count is reported)
output.parse_prose: json field action (expects 'A' or 'B'); fallback regex '"action"\s*:\s*"?([AB])'

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: 100 x (number of valid runs whose action == 'A') / (number of valid runs) over the 800 Stag Hunt A->B Answer-Only runs
metric.original_location: Table 1, row GPT-4-Turbo / A, column SH AO A->B (B = 74.5)

notes: Stochastic statistic at T = 1.0: each seed is a fresh set of 800 draws. The paper's run date is unknown (arXiv July 2024, no snapshot string), so the 2024-04-09 snapshot is the alias-rule resolution. The B->A companion cell (45.6) uses Table 6 configs 3-4 with B listed first. 800 inline rows = 2 payoff configurations x 4 preference pairs x 100 run indices (identical prompts within a setup); fields.label 'expected_action' = 'A' for every row so accuracy x 100 = frequency of choosing A.
